scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2642 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. scenicChapters.title: Col de l Iseran → Col du Galibier
scenicChapters.narrative: Exposed ground: wind matters more here than gradient. Nothing blocks it. Height already gained and held. The road stays near 2764 m for 181 km instead of surrendering it to the next valley.

scenicChapters.title: Col d Izoard → Col de Vars
scenicChapters.narrative: 88 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 78 km. 607 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it. The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1607 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

story: From Thonon-les-Bains it runs 1073 km to Menton; allow about 15 h 27 of riding. It goes by way of Col des Gets, Col des Aravis, Col du Cormet de Roselend and Col de l Iseran. The highest point is about 2,750 m. Cormet de Roselend, Col du Galibier, Col d Izoard, Col de Vars, Col de Restefond and Col de Turini are subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

scenicChapters.title: Pyrenees Cols Route
scenicChapters.narrative: The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 6.5%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter — first and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding.

scenicChapters.title: Pyrenees Cols Route
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1569 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.

story: A one-way ride of 249 km, Lourdes to Saint-Girons - roughly 3 h 25 in the saddle. It goes by way of Col du Tourmalet, Col d Aspin, Col de Peyresourde and Bagneres de Luchon. The highest point is about 2,100 m. Col du Tourmalet, Col d Aspin and Col de Peyresourde are subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 38 km. 1172 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Col des Gets → Col des Aravis
scenicChapters.narrative: This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else. 49 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1967 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

story: A 121 km loop that starts and ends near Thonon-les-Bains, about 1 h 57 of riding. The stops in between: Col des Gets and Col des Aravis. The highest point is about 1,950 m. Cormet de Roselend is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 22 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

story: From Sainte-Marguerite it runs 386 km to Sainte-Marguerite; allow about 6 h 39 of riding. It goes by way of Arles, The Maison Carrée of Nîmes, Pont du Gard and back through Pont du Gard. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
